proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnification section even though Sections 9.3, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists (9.3 cross-refers to Section 20.5). We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data incidents and wilful misconduct, with the usual notice/control procedure and IP remedies; per Section 21.3 indemnification obligations sit outside the liability cap.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor against third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of a claim, the indemnifying Party shall control the defence with counsel of its choice, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. No settlement that imposes a non-monetary obligation or admission on the indemnified Party may be made without its prior written consent.

If an infringement claim is made or reasonably anticipated, Vendor shall at its expense procure the necessary rights, or modify or replace the affected Services or Deliverables with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing alternative; if none is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees and Fees paid for affected Deliverables.

proposal.summary: Insert missing Vendor indemnity as new Section 20 and repair the broken cross-reference in 9.3

quote: Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
rationale: There is no indemnification section at all: the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), yet Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all assume indemnities exist and 9.3 cross-references a non-existent Section 20.5. We inserted a new Section 20 with a Vendor IP/breach-of-law/data-incident/wilful-misconduct indemnity, a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and its breach of law, standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and the procure-modify-replace-refund remedies (which also repairs the 9.3 cross-reference).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so Vendor assigns each Deliverable to us; Vendor keeps its pre-existing Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 with the perpetual licence in Section 13.2. Our fallback is Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.

ops.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each such Deliverable upon creation. To the extent any such assignment is ineffective, Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, transferable licence to use, modify, and sublicense the Deliverable for Customer's business.
ops.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.

proposal.summary: Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; delete the revocable term licence

quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
rationale: Section 14.1 correctly leaves Customer Data and our pre-existing IP with us and 14.4 bars joint ownership, but 14.2 reverses our position on paid-for work product: Vendor owns every Deliverable and we get only a revocable, non-transferable term licence, so we lose access to what we paid for on expiry. We flipped ownership to Customer with an assignment (and a perpetual, irrevocable, transferable fallback licence); Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under 14.3 with the Section 13.2 perpetual licence.

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 matches our preferred position: a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees (paid or payable) and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages with restoration and incident-response costs treated as direct damages, and Excluded Claims in 21.3 covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. "Fees" (1.5) is the full recurring/professional/usage fee stream, so the cap is not illusory, and Customer's payment obligation is expressly not "damages". No redline needed; note that the Excluded Claims reference to "indemnification obligations" only has effect once the missing indemnity (INDEMN) is added.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
rationale: Section 24 tracks our preferred position: Customer may assign freely to an Affiliate or an M&A successor on notice (24.1); Vendor needs our consent for assignment, delegation or change of control and may never assign to a Customer competitor (24.2); other assignments require consent not unreasonably withheld (24.3); and Vendor gets no termination, suspension or repricing right on our change of control (24.4). Section 13.3 consistently permits transfer of licence rights with a permitted assignment. No redline needed.

proposal.summary: Delete the disclose-and-match precondition to engaging another provider

quote: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
rationale: Conditioning our engagement of any other provider on disclosing and matching offers operates as a right of first refusal and de facto exclusive dealing for the full term, with no performance-based exit — our walk-away position, and inconsistent with Section 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement (reinforced by the take-or-pay lock-in in Section 2.1). We deleted the clause.

quote: Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge is payable by Customer anywhere in the Agreement: service credits are referenced only as amounts flowing to us (Section 1.5), Section 7.3 lets us withhold disputed amounts, and Section 27.3 permits termination "without penalty" with a refund. Compliant as drafted; the take-or-pay in Section 2.1 is addressed under MINCOMMIT, and our termination-for-convenience insert states expressly that no early-termination charge applies so it cannot be recharacterised as a penalty.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or further volume or payment obligation, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.summary: Add a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund

quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
rationale: Section 9 provides only termination for breach, insolvency and Vendor performance failures (numbering skips 9.4) — there is no convenience right for Customer in a three-year term, and Section 2.1 expressly denies termination rights, which is our walk-away position. We inserted a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination charge, and confirming Vendor has no mid-term convenience exit.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or exit; we have limited any commitment to the current 12-month term, made it reducible on 30 days' notice, replaced the shortfall with a true-up carry-forward of credits, and confirmed it ends on termination — consistent with Section 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement. Our preference remains deletion, with Fees payable for Services actually ordered.

ops.newText: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase commitment, and Fees are payable only for Services and Deliverables Customer actually orders under an Order Form. If an Order Form states a volume commitment, that commitment applies only to the then-current twelve-month term, may be reduced by Customer on thirty days' written notice, terminates on termination or expiry of the Agreement or the applicable Order Form, and any shortfall is addressed by a credit carried forward to the following period rather than by any penalty or take-or-pay payment.
ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.

quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
rationale: A USD 2,000,000 per year, three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights is our walk-away position and contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment. We replaced it with our fallback: no standing commitment, any Order Form commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, ending on termination, and any shortfall handled by a carry-forward true-up rather than a penalty.

This Section does not restrict either Party from hiring a person who responds to a general advertisement or other general recruitment effort not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or who approaches the hiring Party on an unsolicited basis.
ops.oldText: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.

proposal.summary: Narrow the non-solicit to a mutual, 12-month restriction on involved personnel with advertising carve-out and no no-hire

quote: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
rationale: This is a one-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees and expressly capturing people who apply on their own initiative — our walk-away position. We narrowed it to our fallback: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches, and no "hire or employ" prohibition.

ops.text: On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates and continue the affected Services during that period on the existing terms; (b) within thirty days of Customer's request, return or export all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format at no additional charge; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify the deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and Customer Data return/deletion obligations in Section 10

quote: On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period.
rationale: Section 10 assumes an "agreed transition period" but no clause obliges Vendor to provide exit assistance or to return or export Customer Data in a usable format, and Section 16.5 defers Customer Data to an absent Section 11 — leaving us exposed to loss of access to hosted health data on exit. We inserted a new Section 10.3 requiring up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return/export of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.
